after: The campus is the first CloudBurst Data Centers gigacenter, planned between San Marcos and New Braunfels in Central Texas. CloudBurst is a Denver firm founded in 2022. A Community Impact report from May 2025 puts the site on a 96-acre parcel off Francis Harris Lane that straddles Hays County and Guadalupe County. The full campus is planned at 1.2 GW, with a first 50 MW phase due online in the fourth quarter of 2026. A w.media article from November 2025 says a groundbreaking was held and that no tenant is named. Power would come from a behind-the-meter natural gas plant on site. Energy Transfer agreed to supply up to 450,000 million British thermal units per day for 10 years, and w.media says delivery is through the Oasis Pipeline. Community Impact and Data Center Dynamics say only that the gas comes through a pipeline running through the site. CloudBurst also plans a separate 200 MW site in Oklahoma.

The related data center is the Oracle campus near Abilene, Texas, which is part of the OpenAI Stargate effort. Crusoe is developing it on the 800 acre Lancium Clean Campus and leases about 90 acres. A Data Center Frontier article from March 2025 says the plan is eight buildings, about 4 million square feet and 1.2 GW in total, with the first two buildings over 200 MW. It says construction began in June 2024 and the full build was expected by mid-2026. An Energy Transfer earnings release from the third quarter of 2025 says it signed multiple long-term deals to supply about 900 million cubic feet a day of gas to three Oracle data centers, two of them in Texas. That release does not say how much of the gas goes to Abilene. An Energy Transfer executive quoted in an ETF Trends article from November 2025 calls Oracle a major customer in Abilene. Energy Transfer's second quarter 2026 release reports a second 14-mile lateral off the pipeline in Abilene. Data Center Frontier also says Crusoe lined up 4.5 GW of gas power with Engine No. 1, but does not clearly tie all of it to Abilene.

No single data center campus is named for this project. Williams says the Power Express expansion is aimed at the data center market in Virginia, and the federal Energy Information Administration lists it as serving Northern Virginia data center markets. A Data Center Dynamics article from May 2025 says the project would add 950 million cubic feet per day, with service expected in the third quarter of 2030. Williams says the gas would go to markets north of its compressor station in Chatham, Virginia. Williams has not named a data center developer or tenant. The project was in early development in 2025 and no shipper was named in the sources read.

The pipeline serves a new fuel-cell facility in central Ohio that will give behind-the-meter power to a data center. The Chesapeake Utilities announcement of July 2025 does not name the campus or the customer. The Energy Information Administration pipeline projects workbook of August 2026 describes it as an American Electric Power Ohio data center campus with Amazon Web Services and Cologix as anchor customers. American Electric Power said in June 2025 that the Public Utilities Commission of Ohio approved onsite Bloom Energy solid oxide fuel cells at data centers run by Amazon Web Services and Cologix, which are two customers at what appear to be two sites. A report from the Columbus public radio station WOSU in May 2025 says the Amazon Web Services contract runs six years and the Cologix contract runs 15 years, that the utility would buy gas on the market, and that capacity and site locations were not disclosed. A Data Center Dynamics article from August 2025 says the pipeline is likely to serve a Bloom Energy fuel-cell facility but calls that unconfirmed. The pipeline is due in service in the first half of 2027 and the data center power starts then.

No single data center is named for this project. A Boardwalk press release from December 2024 says the pipeline supplies gas needed to support the growth of data centers and industrial demand, and ties it to electric generation demand in Mississippi and the Southeast. The pipeline is backed by one unnamed anchor customer on a 20-year agreement, and Boardwalk is still negotiating the rest of the capacity. A Hart Energy article from December 2024 repeats that Boardwalk called it a response to growing data center and power generation demand in the Southeast, especially Mississippi. Target in-service is the first half of 2029. No source read ties the pipeline to a specific campus, developer, tenant or power plant.

No single data center campus is named as the customer of this expansion. The Great Basin filing and Nevada Governor Joe Lombardo's February 2026 letter to the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission say it would support existing customers and future economic development, including data centers. A Nevada Current article from June 2026 says the new line would run 14 miles to the Tahoe Regional Industrial Center in Storey County, Nevada. That industrial park has many data center projects but no source ties the pipeline to a specific one. Examples in the park are Fleet Data Centers, owned by Tract, with the Peru Ridge and South Valley campuses, and a Switch campus. A DatacenterDynamics article from September 2026 says Fleet asked for two gas plants totaling 360 MW to run its campuses until NV Energy can supply power. It says one Fleet data center is planned at 230 MW on 256 acres and that the tenant is not named. A Nevada Independent article from June 2026 says Nexus Fulcrum asked to build a 510 MW gas plant at the edge of the park. Switch acquired the site of that plant. None of these articles say they would take gas from this pipeline.

No single data center campus or tenant is named for this project. TC Energy approved the Northwoods expansion in May 2025 at about 900 million dollars to serve gas-fired power generation in the Midwest, including data centers and general economic growth. A Data Center Dynamics article from May 2025 says the added capacity is tied to 20 year take-or-pay contracts with Midwest utilities. A market note from East Daley Analytics, a gas market research firm, says Northwoods and the Guardian expansion together serve data center load growth and new utility generation in Illinois, Wisconsin and Michigan's Upper Peninsula. That note does not name a specific campus. The in-service date is late 2029.

No single data center campus is named for the main line of this pipeline. A North Dakota Monitor article from August 2025 says the pipeline owner told the state that many interested customers are developing power generation to support data centers. A Grand Forks Herald article from August 2025 says company documents show the line could serve 7,000 to 8,000 MW of data center demand. The same article says an 80-mile extension would reach Ellendale in southeastern North Dakota. Ellendale is the home of the Applied Digital Polaris Forge 1 campus, which Applied Digital said in 2025 is fully contracted to CoreWeave for 400 MW with the first 100 MW building at full load. The Herald says Applied Digital is seeking to grow its footprint and energy demand there. Customer agreements are expected in 2026, and the Pipeline and Gas Journal says construction is slated to begin in 2028.

The campus is the Monarch Compute Campus, an artificial intelligence data center in Mason County, West Virginia, near Point Pleasant. A March 2026 press release from American Intelligence and Power Corporation names it as developer and calls the Hope Gas Prosperity Line a component of the campus. Nscale and Fidelis Energy are now named as developers on the Nscale web page and in a WSAZ report from April 2026. Nscale says phase 1 is 1.35 GW of compute with delivery targeted for early 2028 and room to grow to more than 8 GW, on more than 2,250 acres, with more than $20 billion of investment. WSAZ reports a $40 billion figure and operations in the second half of 2027. A Marcellus Drilling News article from March 2026 says an initial 2 GW of power generation would be supported by the pipeline. Nscale says the campus makes all its own power on site with Caterpillar equipment and is independent of the public grid. No tenant is named.

The related data center is Project Jupiter, a hyperscale campus at Santa Teresa in Doña Ana County, New Mexico. Stack and BorderPlex Digital Assets are developing it. Oracle confirmed in January 2026 that it is the tenant and will host AI infrastructure for OpenAI. A DatacenterDynamics article from January 2026 says the campus covers 1,400 acres with four data center buildings, a microgrid, gas power plants, battery storage and a desalination plant. The developers have said they could invest up to $165 billion over the life of the project. Baxtel reported in July 2026 that the campus would run on up to 2.8 GW of Bloom solid oxide fuel cells, and its headline calls the campus 2.5 GW. The Albuquerque Journal says the air permit applicant is Yucca Growth Infrastructure LLC and the campus is under construction. The air permit is still being decided. Source New Mexico reported in April 2026 that the pipeline would carry 400,000 dekatherms a day to the private power plants for the campus, and in August 2026 that its start slipped to early 2027 after the state land office denied a route across state land.
